answer: With bonded collateral escrows, a coordinated set of k identities that equivocates incurs correlated penalties proportional to k² (O(k²)), so splitting one validator across aliases does not dilute exposure. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss makes controlling a larger sybil swarm increasingly costly, while asymmetric depreciation further reduces recovered bonds. Whether named knoll, bridge, or juniper, an identity is not an independent escape route.
